title: Hill climbing with random restarts
sub: Each run climbs from a random start until no neighbour is higher. Keep the best peak found.

frames.caption: A landscape with four peaks. Hill climbing only sees its two neighbours, so it climbs whatever hill it starts on.
Restart 1: start at x = 82, step uphill 7 times, stop at height 0.86: a local peak, but the best so far.
Restart 2: start at x = 38, step uphill 10 times, stop at height 0.63: stuck on a lower peak. The tallest peak's basin is narrow: only 16% of starting points lead there.
Restart 3: start at x = 101, step uphill 26 times, stop at height 0.86: the same peak as before. Wasted run, but cheap.
Restart 4: start at x = 166, step uphill 2 times, stop at height 0.74: stuck on a lower peak. Keep the best and try again.
Restart 5: start at x = 12, step uphill 16 times, stop at height 0.63: stuck on a lower peak. Keep the best and try again.
Restart 6: start at x = 18, step uphill 10 times, stop at height 0.63: stuck on a lower peak. Keep the best and try again.
Restart 7: start at x = 137, step uphill 13 times, stop at height 1.08: it started inside the tall narrow peak's basin of attraction and found the global maximum.
Restart 8: start at x = 24, step uphill 4 times, stop at height 0.63: stuck on a lower peak. Keep the best and try again.
With a 16% chance per run, 8 restarts find the global peak with probability 1 − 0.83<sup>8</sup> = 76%. Restarts are cheap insurance, but the smaller the basin, the more you need.
